subject: AI processing boundaries and subprocessor migration - contract ask
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@healthsync.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: no-training commitment + subprocessor change notice

Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team has one remaining set of asks before procurement can sign: primarily around AI/LLM processing boundaries and controls. I have attached an initial redline that highlights the commercial language we would like to see in the DPA. High level asks below: 

- No model training on HealthSync inputs without explicit written consent (we need an explicit no-training commitment and a workflow for any future exception).
- Ownership and licensing of prompts and model responses: HealthSync must retain rights to customer-provided prompts and to the unredacted responses for audit.
- Subprocessor transparency and migration notice: we need 30 days notice before moving data to any new subprocessor or cloud region, and evidence that onshore processing is available for PHI workloads.
- Evidence pack: SOC 2 Type II, KMS configuration (onshore key residency options), and an operations checklist showing ephemeral KV behavior and retention.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to the no-training language in Section 5 of our redline and provide the evidence matrix referenced above? I attached the redline (HealthSync_Redlines_v1.docx).

Best,
Asha
Legal Ops
HealthSync, Inc.

[Attachment: HealthSync_Redlines_v1.docx (docx, 82KB)]

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@healthsync.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: no-training commitment + subprocessor change notice

Asha,

Thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the redline. Short answers up front: yes, we support a customer-driven no-training commitment and can operationalize a bounded workflow for exceptions; we can provide the evidence you listed and a migration notice policy; and we can propose contract language that preserves your ownership of prompts and responses. I have looped in Marissa and Karthik to coordinate the evidence pack and legal/ops implications.

Operational notes we will include in the evidence matrix:
- No-training opt-out: we will mark HealthSync’s tenant with a no-training flag at the ingestion layer and disable model improvement paths for that tenant. This applies to online learning and any periodic model-tuning jobs.
- Ephemeral KV and prefix caching: KV cache is ephemeral per session and expires after 24 hours by default; we will document retention settings and options for stricter TTLs.
- Onshore processing: we can route HealthSync production traffic to US-only regions and provide SFTP exports or API data pulls for exportability.
- Subprocessor notice: standard is 30 days for critical subprocessors; we will add a contractual 30-day migration notice for any new subprocessor that would handle customer data.

Next steps from our side: Marissa will prepare the evidence matrix (SOC 2, KMS config notes, ops checklist) and Dev will confirm the implementation timeline for the no-train flag and onshore routing. Would HealthSync prefer we propose precise contract wording or mark up your redline?

Jonas
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

--

Asha,

Appreciate the patience while we pulled the right folks together. Attached is the evidence matrix and a short proposed contract snippet that mirrors the language you requested. Highlights below and answers inline to the redline: 

1) No-training commitment (Section 5)
- Proposed snippet: 
  Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, improve, or otherwise update any machine learning model used in production to serve Customer requests without the Customer's prior written consent. Customer Data will be logically marked in our ingestion layer as exempt from model improvement jobs. Exceptions require written approval from an authorized Customer contact and will be subject to a documented exception review.
- Implementation: we will persist a tenant-level no-train flag. We tested the flag in staging; production rollout for new tenants can be completed within 7 business days after contract signature. Existing tenants will require a short activation window (1-2 business days) after we toggle the flag.

2) Prompt and response ownership
- We confirm that Customer retains ownership of customer-provided prompts and raw responses. Redwood will not assert downstream IP claims over customer inputs or outputs. We are proposing specific language in the attached contract snippet.

3) Subprocessor migration notice and onshore processing
- Notice: Redwood will provide at least thirty (30) days prior written notice before onboarding any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data.
- Onshore routing: For PHI-designated workloads, we can pin processing to US-only regions. There is no need for new third-party subprocessors for routing; it is a configuration in our routing layer.

4) Evidence pack
- Attached: no-train-evidence-matrix.xlsx with SOC 2 Type II summary, KMS configuration notes, and the ops playbook checklist for KV behavior, retention, and export steps. We can add screenshots or sanitized configs as needed for procurement.

Attachments: HealthSync_Redlines_v1.docx (received), no-train-evidence-matrix.xlsx (attached).

If this works for you we can produce a marked-up DPA with the proposed snippets in place tonight and arrange a short call early next week to walk legal through the tech bits.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
